title: heterogeneous-gpu-mixing-scaling-observations
content:
Summary:
This note captures an exploratory investigation into mixing dissimilar GPUs in a single multi-GPU serving group and the impact on tensor/pipeline parallel workloads. The goal was to reproduce a customer-reported throughput regression when an older A100-40GB node was introduced into an otherwise homogeneous A100-80GB cluster, and to understand how NCCL/allreduce, NVLink topologies, and pipeline scheduling interact to cause backpressure and kernel serialization.

High-level findings (short):
- Mixing GPUs with different compute and memory characteristics produced non-linear throughput degradation (~20–45% drop vs homogeneous baseline) even though peak FLOPS gap was ~15%.
- Major bottleneck observed was cross-device synchronization and unexpected CPU-side staggers at end-of-step collective calls; communication accounted for 60–80% of step time in worst cases.
- NVLink-connected pairs masked some heterogeneity, but any allreduce spanning NVLink boundaries into PCIe/IB paths amplified stalls due to different per-rank progress rates.
- Pipeline parallel schedules exacerbate the effect: slow micro-batches at certain pipeline stages create head-of-line blocking for subsequent stages.

Experiment matrix and environment:
- Software: CUDA 12.1, cuDNN 9.2, NCCL 2.16.6, PyTorch 2.2 nightly from infra build, nsys 2024.3.2 for traces.
- Hardware topologies tested:
  - Baseline: 4x A100-80GB on single node with full NVLink mesh (homogeneous).
  - Mixed-1: 3x A100-80GB + 1x A100-40GB on same node (NVLink partially connecting 40GB GPU to only two neighbors).
  - Mixed-2: 2x A100-80GB (node A) + 2x A10 (node B) across HDR200 InfiniBand (RoCE v2).
- Models/workloads:
  - GPT-like decoder-only, 2B parameter sharded with tensor-parallel=2, pipeline-parallel=2, micro-batch size 1 per micro-step. Sequence length 1024.
  - Batch-limited evaluation mode (low concurrency) to emphasize per-step synchronization.
- Metrics captured: per-step latency (p50/p95), tokens/s, per-rank kernel time breakdown, NCCL trace events (collStart/collEnd), PCIe memcpy durations, GPU occupancy, and host-side queueing.

Profile observations (detailed):
- Baseline (4x A100-80GB): tokens/s = 1200, step p95 ≈ 35ms, collectives ~18% of step time. Kernel timelines show overlapping compute and comm using CUDA streams; nvtx tags show well-formed pipelining.

- Mixed-1 (single-node, one A100-40GB): tokens/s dropped to 820 (≈32% drop). Trace highlights:
  - One rank shows consistently longer GEMM kernels (approx +12% per-kernel) due to lower sustained memory bandwidth and slightly different SASS code paths in cuBLAS for 40GB SKU.
  - NCCL allreduce for KV cache and attention softmax had long tail: collStart/collEnd delta for groups including the 40GB rank increased by 2.2x.
  - NVLink partial connectivity: the 40GB card only had links to two neighbors; some allreduce phases had to route via PCIe, causing additional host involvement.
  - Host CPU indicated bursts of memcpy calls blocking on pinned buffer allocation; correlated with spikes in host-side latency preceding collectives.

- Mixed-2 (cross-node A100/A10): tokens/s = 660 (≈45% drop vs baseline). Observations:
  - A10 nodes had lower FP16 throughput and smaller L2 caches; compute time per micro-batch increased by ~30%.
  - RDMA layer (Mellanox HDR200) introduced consistent per-call latency but main issue was unbalanced progress: faster ranks wait at MPI/NCCL barrier for slower ranks leading to poor overlap between compute and comm.
  - NCCL algorithm chosen was ring-by-default; ring latency amplified when hops include an A10 (slower). Switching to NCCL_ALGO=Tree reduced worst-case latency by ~12% but did not recover throughput to baseline.

Root causes and mechanism hypothesis:
1) Progress imbalance: In mixed groups, different per-rank compute durations cause the faster GPUs to enter collectives earlier and then wait. NCCL's progress model and rendezvous sizes cause head-of-line blocking where later hops cannot start until earlier hops finish (visible in ring traces).
2) Interconnect heterogeneity: NVLink mesh differences force some collective traffic to traverses PCIe or IB, incurring higher latency and added CPU involvement.
3) Kernels and resource contention: cuBLAS/cuDNN select slightly different kernels across GPU models; fused ops and workspace sizes differ, creating small divergences which compound across many micro-steps.
4) Pipeline amplification: pipeline-parallel scheduling creates strict ordering; a slow micro-batch at stage 1 stalls downstream stages even if they could have overlapped work.

Mitigations tested and results:
- Per-rank compute padding: artificially inserting sleep in faster ranks to align with slowest rank recovered ~70% of lost throughput but is wasteful.
- NCCL tuning: setting NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and trying NCCL_BUFFSIZE=8MB gave minor improvements; forcing NCCL_ALGO=Tree helped latency tails but throughput gains limited.
- Topology-aware placement: keeping pipeline stages and tensor-parallel peers on NVLink-connected subsets reduced cross-path collectives; mixed groups segmented into homogeneous subgroups gave best results (tokens/s ~1050).
- Dynamic micro-batch sizing: reducing micro-batch on slower ranks lowered imbalance but required changes in model code to support heterogeneous micro-batch – further work required.

Actionable recommendations for infra and runtime:
- Prevent mixing GPUs with notably different sustained memory bandwidth or compute capability in a single NCCL process group used for synchronous collectives. Enforce placement constraints in scheduler.
- Add a topology-aware group formation logic in runtime: form collectives preferentially over NVLink meshes, fall back to cross-node only for aggregation phases (e.g., use hierarchical allreduce: intra-node then inter-node).
- Expose a runtime option to choose NCCL algorithm per collective size and topology (auto-tune profile cache).
- Instrument per-rank progress metrics (simple piggyback counters) and surface in Console so users can detect imbalance due to heterogeneity.
- Explore asynchronous offloading of small collectives or using finer-grained kv-cache caching to reduce frequency of large allreduces.

Planned follow-ups / experiments:
- Microbench suite: systematic allreduce latency/throughput sweep across message sizes (128B..32MB) with heterogeneous pairs (A100-80 vs A100-40 vs A10) to map thresholds where algorithm selection flips. (JIRA-2081)
- RDMA tuning: test RoCEv2 vs Connected Transport and varying MTU; measure effect on NCCL ring hops spanning nodes.
- Kernel dive: capture cuBLASSASS traces for divergent GEMM kernels between SKUs and see whether different workspace sizes cause asynchronous cudaMalloc stalls.
- Scheduler PoC: implement a scheduler flag to avoid placing different SKU GPUs in same model group; rollback policy and experiment on dedicated infra.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why do host memcpy stalls appear correlated with collectives only for the mixed-1 case? Hypothesis: partially-pinned buffers and fallback staging on CPU when NVLink doesn't cover path; need to check driver trace and page-lock counts.
- Can runtime heuristics detect and automatically re-shard tensor parallel groups to equalize work without application changes?
- Impact on latency-sensitive small-batch serving: our experiments are batch-limited; small-batch/streaming behavior may differ.

Notes to reviewers:
- I attached nsys timeline snapshots and a short script to reproduce Mixed-1 here: https://git.redwood.com/repo/infra/pr/784 (see run/mixed-1).
- If we need a quick mitigation for Dedicated cluster customers, recommend scheduling policy to avoid heterogeneous mixing for production model groups while we implement hierarchical collectives.

Appendix (quick commands used):
- nsys profile --output=trace.nsys ./run_inference --tp 2 --pp 2 --micro-batch 1
- sudo nvidia-smi topo -m  # NVLink/PCIe topology
- NCCL debug: NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=ALL python run.py

End of note.
